newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: QNI blames weather, prices for profit fall.
newsitem.headline: QNI blames weather, prices for profit fall.

text.p: Nickel producer QNI Ltd said on Monday its sharp profit fall for the year to June 30, 1997 was due mainly to continuing volatility in the nickel and cobalt markets and cyclonic weather conditions.
QNI earlier reported a 1996/97 net profit of A$32.11 million, compared with A$85.89 million a year ago.
Sales revenue fell 24 percent to A$312.7 million.
QNI chairman Max Roberts said the demand for primary nickel did not grow as expected during 1996/97 due to subdued growth in demand for stainless steel and the availability of stainless steel scrap.
The average annual London Metal Exchange cash nickel price for the year was US$3.27 a pound, down US$0.45 on the previous year, Roberts said in a statement accompanying the group's results.
He expected nickel price volatility to continue in the short term.
The cobalt market had been less volatile and was enjoying modest demand, but remained susceptible to "price weakness" below current levels of US$20 a pound, Roberts said.

"Disruptions to ore supply included poor weather conditions and industrial unrest at some mine sites but we expect this situation to improve in the coming year and ore stockpiles at Yabulu refinery are now replenished," he said.
QNI's Yabulu refinery in Queensland produces about 30,000 tonnes of nickel and 2,000 tonns of cobalt a year.
QNI announced in June a plan to merge its nickel operations with Gencor Ltd's Billiton Nickel.
The plan has met opposition from institutional shareholders, despite a revised proposal unveiled earlier this month.
QNI's shares closed down seven cents at A$2.11 in a declining market.
